nodes.label: Consistency first (project conventions win)
nodes.author: laravel
nodes.rationale: A pattern repeated throughout the project is a convention and takes precedence over this skill; an existing test that follows a convention is not defective.

nodes.label: Feature test first
nodes.author: laravel
nodes.rationale: Most behavior is reachable through a request; write a unit test only for logic that does not use the framework.

nodes.label: Test observable behavior and contracts
nodes.author: laravel
nodes.rationale: A test must pass after an implementation change if the behavior stays the same; cover every changed decision and each high-value failure mode.

nodes.label: Tailwind v4 CSS-first @theme configuration
nodes.author: laravel
nodes.rationale: Tailwind v4 moves configuration into CSS via the @theme directive and drops tailwind.config.js and corePlugins support; imports use @import "tailwindcss" instead of the v3 @tailwind directives.

nodes.label: Record decisions, not defaults test
nodes.author: laravel
nodes.rationale: A convention earns a rule only when it reflects a real fork the next agent would not default to by itself; framework defaults and active-tool target forms are skipped, while against-the-grain holds and architecture choices are the gold.

nodes.label: Consistency First principle
nodes.author: laravel
nodes.rationale: Inconsistency is worse than a suboptimal pattern; the pattern the codebase already uses wins over theoretically better alternatives, so rules are defaults for when no pattern exists yet.

nodes.label: Tailwind v4 CSS-first configuration (@theme)
nodes.author: laravel
nodes.rationale: In v4 configuration lives in CSS via @theme; corePlugins and a separate tailwind.config.js are not supported.

nodes.label: Exception report()/render() pattern
nodes.rationale: Exception methods keep behavior beside the exception definition; centralized callbacks in bootstrap/app.php keep the application's exception policy together.

nodes.label: Exception report throttling (throttle/Lottery/Limit)
nodes.rationale: A failing integration can flood logs or error tracking; sample or rate-limit matching exception reports.

nodes.label: shouldRenderJsonWhen JSON policy for API routes
nodes.norm_label: shouldrenderjsonwhen json policy for api routes

nodes.label: Event discovery for listeners
nodes.rationale: Laravel discovers listeners by inspecting type-hinted event arguments on handle()/__invoke(); register manually only when discovery is disabled or unclear.

nodes.label: Events and Notifications Best Practices (Laravel rules)
nodes.norm_label: events and notifications best practices (laravel rules)

nodes.label: Explicit HTTP error handling (throw/successful/notFound)
nodes.rationale: The HTTP client returns responses for 4xx/5xx instead of throwing; inspect expected statuses or call throw() before consuming a success payload.

nodes.label: Retry only safe operations (idempotency keys)
nodes.rationale: A retried state-changing request can duplicate the operation unless the remote API supports an idempotency key or equivalent duplicate protection.

nodes.label: Separate content and delivery mail tests
nodes.norm_label: separate content and delivery mail tests

nodes.label: Honest migration rollbacks (down())
nodes.rationale: A rollback that drops populated columns or cannot restore transformed data is destructive even if syntactically reversible.

nodes.label: Deployed migrations are immutable
nodes.rationale: Editing a migration that already ran in production makes fresh installations differ from upgraded installations.

nodes.label: Design indexes for real queries
nodes.rationale: A column in WHERE, ORDER BY, or JOIN does not automatically need its own index; base indexes on query patterns, selectivity, and write cost.

nodes.label: Stage changes affecting existing rows
nodes.rationale: Adding a required or unique column to a populated table needs nullable-first, code that handles both states, bounded backfill, then the constraint.

nodes.label: Back off transient failures ($tries/$backoff)
nodes.rationale: Progressively longer delays give a dependency time to recover; permanent validation or business-rule failures must not be retried.

nodes.label: Bus::batch job batching
nodes.rationale: A batch is not a database transaction: completed jobs are not rolled back when another job fails.

nodes.label: Job failed() terminal handling
nodes.rationale: Laravel invokes failed() on a new job instance, so mutations made during handle() are not available there.

nodes.label: Queue and Job Best Practices (Laravel rules)
nodes.norm_label: queue and job best practices (laravel rules)

nodes.label: Resource-oriented controller organization
nodes.rationale: A focused resource controller gives a custom behavior its own authorization, validation, and middleware boundary; treat a custom verb as a design signal.

nodes.label: Bound work inside the scheduled task
nodes.norm_label: bound work inside the scheduled task
nodes.rationale: The scheduler does not terminate arbitrary tasks at a deadline; bound work via finite chunks, deadline checks, or queue jobs with timeouts.

nodes.label: withoutOverlapping lock
nodes.rationale: The optional value is the lock expiration time in minutes, not the task timeout; the default is 24 hours, and a too-short expiration can permit overlap.

nodes.label: CSRF protection (@csrf / X-XSRF-TOKEN)
nodes.rationale: Routes intentionally excluded from CSRF verification, such as validated third-party webhooks, need their own authenticity check.

nodes.label: Bind query parameters (no SQL interpolation)
nodes.rationale: Bindings protect values, not identifiers such as column names or sort directions; map user-selected identifiers to an allow-list.

nodes.label: assertSame over assertEquals
nodes.rationale: assertSame also compares the type, so a string 1 does not silently pass against an integer 1.

nodes.label: Correlated subquery pattern
nodes.rationale: Selecting a single has-many value through a correlated subquery with addSelect() avoids loading the entire relationship; whether EXISTS, IN, join, or two simple queries is fastest depends on the database engine and query plan, so measure.

nodes.label: Global scope tradeoff
nodes.rationale: Global scopes silently modify every query on a model, hiding rows from admin panels, reports, and jobs; reserve them for truly universal constraints like soft deletes or multi-tenancy.

nodes.label: Deployed migrations are immutable
nodes.rationale: Editing a migration that already ran in a shared environment makes fresh installations diverge from upgraded ones, so subsequent changes ship as new migrations.

nodes.label: Staged column addition and backfill
nodes.rationale: Adding a required or unique column to a populated table is not one safe step: add nullable, deploy dual-state code, backfill in bounded chunks, then add the constraint; large backfills belong in restartable commands, not schema migrations.

nodes.label: Named response assertions (assertNotFound over assertStatus 404)
nodes.rationale: A named assertion failure identifies the broken contract rather than just a status number.

nodes.label: Endpoint coverage case matrix
nodes.rationale: Cover missing/invalid auth, cross-tenant requests, insufficient role, constraint failure, validation failure, and the valid case with response plus persisted state.

nodes.label: Search docs before hand-rolling test code
nodes.norm_label: search docs before hand-rolling test code
nodes.rationale: Do not write an API you have not confirmed in the docs for the installed version.

nodes.label: LazilyRefreshDatabase over RefreshDatabase
nodes.rationale: A test that does not use the database then does not run the migrations.

nodes.label: Real queries against real test-database records
nodes.norm_label: real queries against real test-database records
nodes.rationale: Mocking the query builder makes the test assert the mock; test application behavior caused by the schema, not the engine's cascade implementation.

nodes.label: Parallel runs with ParaTest (php artisan test --parallel)
nodes.norm_label: parallel runs with paratest (php artisan test --parallel)
nodes.rationale: A parallel run gives each process a separate database; a test that fails only in parallel depends on order, shared records, or a shared resource.

nodes.label: Test environment settings (BCRYPT_ROUNDS/WithCachedConfig/withoutVite)
nodes.rationale: With the default BCRYPT_ROUNDS of 12 the hash takes most of the time of each test that signs a user in; measure before changing any setting.

nodes.label: Test review checklist
nodes.rationale: A passing test may still provide no value; for each test, identify the defect it would catch.

nodes.label: Security boundary testing
nodes.rationale: A defect at a boundary where user input affects authorization, output, or queries is hard to detect because the feature may keep working.

nodes.label: Named factory states over raw attributes
nodes.norm_label: named factory states over raw attributes
nodes.rationale: A named state gives the data meaning; a raw attribute array gives only its value.

nodes.label: Each test makes its own data
nodes.norm_label: each test makes its own data
nodes.rationale: Records created in setUp() remain in memory until the suite ends; per-test creation keeps setup visible and lets each test choose its factory state.

nodes.label: Atomic locks for race conditions
nodes.rationale: Concurrent execution that must be serialized needs a lock: Cache::lock() for atomic cross-process coordination, lockForUpdate() for database rows inside a transaction; the two solve different coordination problems.

nodes.label: Cache-aside read via Cache::remember()
nodes.rationale: A manual truthiness check treats valid falsy values like false or 0 as cache misses; Cache::remember() implements cache-aside correctly, though it does not prevent duplicate computation under concurrency.

nodes.label: Bus::batch group coordination
nodes.rationale: A batch is not a database transaction: completed jobs are not rolled back when another job fails, so allowFailures() is a deliberate choice for partial-failure tolerance.

nodes.label: ShouldBeUnique dispatch deduplication
nodes.rationale: Uniqueness uses a shared cache lock and is not a substitute for idempotent processing or a database constraint; it deduplicates dispatch, not execution.

nodes.label: withoutOverlapping() overlap prevention
nodes.rationale: A second run must not begin while the previous holds the lock; the optional value is lock expiration in minutes, and an expiration too short permits overlap while the first task still runs.

nodes.label: env() only in config files
nodes.rationale: Once configuration is cached Laravel does not load .env, so application code reading env() breaks in production; read values through config() instead.

nodes.label: Mass assignment protection via $fillable
nodes.rationale: Mass-assignment protection controls which attributes create()/fill()/update() may set; it does not validate values or authorize the operation, and $guarded = [] opts out entirely.

nodes.label: Rate limiting of sensitive endpoints
nodes.rationale: An IP-only key unfairly groups users behind shared networks while an account-only key enables targeted denial of service, so choose limiter keys deliberately; rate limiting reduces abuse but does not replace authentication or authorization.

nodes.label: Idempotency keys for safe retries
nodes.rationale: Retries can duplicate state-changing requests; only retry non-idempotent calls when the remote API supports an idempotency key or equivalent duplicate protection, sending a stable key on every attempt.

nodes.norm_label: rbac roles (super admin, hq admin, branch admin, branch manager, management, auditor)

nodes.label: ULID Internal IDs (business numbers not PKs)
nodes.norm_label: ulid internal ids (business numbers not pks)

nodes.label: Authorization of protected actions
nodes.rationale: Authentication alone does not establish permission and validation is not authorization; public actions intentionally available to everyone do not need a redundant check.

nodes.label: Form Request validation boundary
nodes.rationale: Extract a form request when validation or authorization is substantial, reused, or clearer outside the controller; validation establishes the shape of input and does not itself authorize the user, and validated data is still not automatically safe for mass assignment.

nodes.label: Constructor dependency injection preference
nodes.rationale: app()/resolve() service location hides dependencies; constructor or method injection makes them explicit and testable.

nodes.label: lazy() vs cursor() iteration tradeoffs
nodes.rationale: Offset pagination in lazy()/chunk() lets row updates shift results and skip or repeat records; lazyById()/chunkById() paginate by a monotonic key and are safer when updating during iteration.

nodes.label: N+1 query prevention via eager loading
nodes.norm_label: n+1 query prevention via eager loading
nodes.rationale: Accessing a relationship per model runs one query per model; with() eager loading collapses the pattern into an initial query plus one relationship query.

nodes.label: Model::preventLazyLoading development guard
nodes.rationale: Enabling preventLazyLoading outside production throws LazyLoadingViolationException on accidental lazy access, surfacing N+1 issues during development instead of production.

nodes.label: ShouldDispatchAfterCommit
nodes.rationale: An event dispatched inside a database transaction should not fire if the transaction rolls back; ShouldDispatchAfterCommit delays dispatch until all open transactions commit, affecting both synchronous and queued listeners.

nodes.norm_label: validation and forms best practices (laravel rules)

nodes.label: Validation message testing per rule
nodes.rationale: A message that is present but wrong is a defect; assert the text the user gets, not that a rules array contains a string.

nodes.label: Data providers for parameterized cases
nodes.rationale: One test function with a branch in the body is two tests in one function; use a provider when setup, body, and assertions stay the same across values.

nodes.label: Global Fakes in Base TestCase setUp()
nodes.norm_label: global fakes in base testcase setup()

nodes.label: Action Classes for Focused Business Operations
nodes.norm_label: action classes for focused business operations

nodes.label: lazyById() for Safe Iteration While Updating
nodes.norm_label: lazybyid() for safe iteration while updating

nodes.label: ShouldDispatchAfterCommit
nodes.rationale: An event dispatched inside a transaction that rolls back would reference data that no longer exists; delay dispatch until commit.

nodes.label: Mailable afterCommit dispatch
nodes.rationale: A queued mailable dispatched during a transaction can be processed before the commit and reference rolled-back records.

nodes.label: Delivery mode assertions (assertQueued vs assertSent)
nodes.rationale: A mailable implementing ShouldQueue is queued even when the call site uses Mail::send(), so assertSent would fail.

nodes.label: Framework fakes for facades
nodes.rationale: A framework fake preserves the real code path while a mock replaces the dependency; create fakes inside the test method, not in setUp().

nodes.label: Global fakes in base TestCase setUp
nodes.norm_label: global fakes in base testcase setup
nodes.rationale: One request that reaches the network can slow the whole suite; preventStrayRequests, Sleep::fake, and Exceptions::fake belong in the base setUp.

nodes.label: Controllers focused on HTTP concerns
nodes.rationale: Extract substantial or reusable business logic, but do not introduce an action or service merely to satisfy an arbitrary line limit.

nodes.label: Validate and store uploads safely
nodes.rationale: The mimes rule reads file contents and guesses a MIME type; it does not validate the user-assigned filename extension, so pair it with the extensions rule.

nodes.label: Form request extraction at the boundary
nodes.norm_label: form request extraction at the boundary
nodes.rationale: Use a form request when validation or authorization is substantial, reused, or clearer outside the controller; inline validate() stays fine for small endpoint-specific rules.

nodes.label: Collaborator Isolation Fork (Mockery vs real integration)
nodes.norm_label: collaborator isolation fork (mockery vs real integration)

nodes.label: Composite Index Design for the Query
nodes.norm_label: composite index design for the query

nodes.label: View Composers for Shared View Data
nodes.norm_label: view composers for shared view data

nodes.label: Keep Queries Out of Blade Templates
nodes.norm_label: keep queries out of blade templates

nodes.label: Queued notifications (ShouldQueue + Queueable)
nodes.rationale: Notifications that call external services such as email, text, or Slack need not complete before the response.

nodes.label: Explicit HTTP timeouts (connectTimeout/timeout)
nodes.rationale: The default 30-second timeout rarely fits the service, and retries can multiply total elapsed time.

nodes.label: retry_after longer than job execution
nodes.rationale: When a reservation expires, another worker can reserve the same job while the first process is still running; keep --timeout several seconds shorter than retry_after.

nodes.label: Fake HTTP requests in tests (Http::fake/preventStrayRequests)
nodes.rationale: Also test timeouts, connection failures, and error responses that the application handles, not only the happy path.

nodes.label: Outbound HTTP testing (Http::preventStrayRequests)
nodes.rationale: A fake without an endpoint accepts unexpected requests and can hide defects; fake the exact endpoint each test uses.

nodes.label: DB constraints for race-prone invariants
nodes.rationale: Validation against mutable state does not prevent a race between validation and persistence; enforce invariants with database constraints, atomic updates, or a transaction.

nodes.label: RateLimited queue middleware
nodes.rationale: Jobs that share a third-party API quota need rate limiting; released attempts may still count toward the attempt limit.

nodes.label: Rate limit sensitive endpoints (RateLimiter::for)
nodes.rationale: An IP address alone can unfairly group users behind a shared network, while an account identifier alone can enable targeted denial of service.

nodes.label: ShouldBeUnique dispatch deduplication (uniqueId/uniqueFor)
nodes.rationale: Uniqueness uses a cache lock and is not a substitute for idempotent processing or a database constraint.

nodes.label: onOneServer single-node execution
nodes.rationale: Scheduler nodes must share the same default cache store, and that store must support atomic locks.

nodes.label: Authorize protected actions (gates/policies/form requests)
nodes.rationale: Authentication alone does not establish permission, and validation is not authorization.

nodes.label: Test authorization at the policy level
nodes.norm_label: test authorization at the policy level
nodes.rationale: An HTTP test cannot identify which mechanism refused the request because middleware, a policy, and abort() can all return 403.

nodes.label: Escape output in its context (Blade {{ }})
nodes.rationale: The raw echo directive is safe only for content sanitized for the exact HTML context; escaping rules differ for HTML, URLs, JavaScript, and CSS.

nodes.label: Escaping test for user-provided content
nodes.rationale: Assert that dangerous characters are escaped and the raw value is absent; do not assert an exact entity for a quote, because Markdown and mail CSS inliners may decode it.

nodes.label: Mass assignment control ($fillable/$guarded)
nodes.rationale: Laravel models guard all attributes by default; $guarded = [] opts out of that protection and must never receive untrusted request data.

nodes.label: Use only intended validated data (validated/safe)
nodes.rationale: Validated data is not automatically safe for mass assignment; keep $fillable/$guarded aligned and never add a sensitive attribute to validation for convenience.

nodes.label: Project naming conventions
nodes.rationale: Prefer Laravel's conventions in new code, but preserve an established project convention unless a coordinated rename is worthwhile.

nodes.label: Test method naming states result and condition
nodes.norm_label: test method naming states result and condition
nodes.rationale: The name of a test method is a specification; test_store() and test_it_works() state no result.

nodes.label: Assert the complete result of a write
nodes.norm_label: assert the complete result of a write
nodes.rationale: A test that asserts only a 200 passes even when the application saves no record; assert response, database state, jobs/events, and mail/notifications, and assert none of these change on the failure path.

nodes.label: Framework assertions over hand-built checks
nodes.rationale: A hand-built check fails with a generic boolean message that identifies nothing; a framework assertion names the incorrect table, value, or response.

nodes.label: Tenant isolation returns 404 not 403
nodes.rationale: A 403 confirms that another tenant's record exists; a 404 does not.
